title: Correlation-Based Measurement of Entanglement in Rank-2 Mixed States
authors: M. I. Samar, V. M. Tkachuk
abstract: We study correlation-based entanglement evaluation in rank-2 mixed states of two- and multi-qubit systems. The relevant two-dimensional subspace is treated as a logical qubit embedded in the physical Hilbert space, and factorizable realizations of its logical Pauli operators are classified. For two qubits, this yields nontrivial canonical encodings related by local Clifford transformations. The relation between logical and physical Bloch vectors admits a geometric interpretation as a transversely deformed Bloch sphere, leading to closed-form expressions for two-qubit concurrence and generalized concurrence across $N$-qubit bipartitions. The entanglement scaling factor is obtained directly from complementary-subsystem correlations, without prior calibration of state-preparation parameters. Noisy simulations using the IBM Quantum FakeKingston backend model, with readout-error mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation, confirm the analytical results up to $N=10$ qubits. The protocol therefore enables entanglement estimation from only a small number of measurement settings for this class of rank-2 logical states.
summary: This paper develops a correlation-based method to estimate entanglement (concurrence) in mixed quantum states by restricting the analysis to rank-2 states. It derives analytical formulas for both two- and multi-qubit systems using only measurements of Pauli correlations. The results are validated against noisy simulations, demonstrating a robust protocol for entanglement estimation with minimal experimental overhead.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately quantifying entanglement in mixed quantum states, specifically focusing on rank-2 mixed states in multi-qubit systems.
main_result: They derive closed-form, correlation-based expressions for concurrence and generalized concurrence for these states, which can be estimated using only a small number of Pauli correlation measurements.
method: The method leverages the structure of rank-2 states, mapping the problem onto a logical qubit description whose Pauli operators admit factorizable physical realizations. Entanglement is then calculated using measurable Pauli expectation values.

paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the theoretical framework for rank-2 states and their logical encoding. It then derives the analytical formulas for concurrence in the two-qubit and general $N$-qubit cases, followed by validation through noisy simulations using error mitigation techniques.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Unified circuit for preparation and measurement of the two-qubit logical states. The binary parameters l, m ∈{0, 1} select Case I (l = 0, m = 1), Case II (l = 1, m = 1), or Case III (l = 1, m = 0). The rotation Rc ∈{I, Rx(π/2), Ry(−π/2)} selects the measurement basis.

Figure 2: Reconstructed concurrence C(ρ) as a function of the mixing parameter p for θ ∈{π/6, π/4, π/3, π/2}. Lines show the exact results, while filled symbols represent noisy simulations using the FakeKingston backend model. Different line styles and marker shapes correspond to different values of θ.

Figure 3: Schematic N-qubit state-preparation and measurement circuit. The first qubit is prepared by U(ai, bi) and entangled with the remaining qubits of subsystem A by CNOT gates. The qubits of subsystem B are prepared by U(θj, ϕj) and coupled to the first qubit through controlled-Z gates. For the measurement of Rx, Rc = Ry(−π/2), while for Ry, Rc = Rx(π/2). The remaining qubits of subsystem A are rotated by Ry(−π/2), and the qubits of subsystem B are measured directly in the computational basis.

Figure 4: Concurrence C(ρ) as a function of p for uniform and mixed angle configurations. Lines show the exact results and filled symbols the error-mitigated FakeKingston simulations. For N = 5, readout mitigation is used, whereas for N = 10 it is supplemented by linear ZNE.
Figure 5: Representative comparison of the exact, raw, and mitigated concurrence. For N = 5, only readout mitigation is applied, while for N = 10 linear ZNE is additionally included.
